extracted.intended_audience: NLP/ML researchers and engineers developing or evaluating automated peer-review / review-generation systems
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and production guidelines for LLM-generated peer reviews and standardized review summaries (decision prediction, review text, and standardized templates), using automatic metrics, a mismatch/regression score, and human/GPT questionnaires. Covers both what to generate (format/content) and how to evaluate quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy (decision prediction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy of generated decisions compared to final Area Chair (AC) decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculated as percent of generated accept/reject decisions that match the final decision (used in Table 4). Interpretation: high accuracy indicates overall alignment with AC decisions, but can be inflated by skewed acceptance rates (e.g., 95% accept rate in a test set).

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision (decision prediction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Precision of generated accept decisions relative to final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precision measures proportion of papers predicted as accepted that were actually accepted. Low precision with high recall indicates tendency to accept many papers (pleasing/lenient behaviour). Useful to detect models that over-accept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recall (decision prediction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recall of generated accept decisions relative to final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recall measures proportion of truly accepted papers that the model predicted as accepted. High recall with low precision suggests the model favors acceptance; interpret jointly with precision and F1.

rubrics_metrics.name: F1-score (decision prediction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Harmonic mean of precision and recall for decision predictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines precision and recall into single summary; useful to compare overall decision-selection performance across models when class balance varies.

rubrics_metrics.name: BERTScore (semantic similarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: BERTScore to measure semantic similarity between generated reasons and meta-reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess semantic alignment of generated textual reasons with human meta-reviews (higher is better). Used alongside classification metrics to capture content-level similarity rather than only label agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: BLEU (text generation)
rubrics_metrics.description: BLEU score of generated reviews/standardized content against references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported (Table 9) as percent; useful for n-gram overlap comparison but limited for abstractive review generation. Should be interpreted with ROUGE and semantic metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUGE (Recall: R-1, R-2, R-L)
rubrics_metrics.description: ROUGE recall metrics (R-1, R-2, R-L) comparing generated text to references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures n-gram and longest-common-subsequence recall; useful to see how much reference content is covered. Used together with ROUGE F1 and BLEU to assess content overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUGE (F1: R-1, R-2, R-L)
rubrics_metrics.description: ROUGE F1 metrics (R-1, R-2, R-L) comparing generated text to references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances precision and recall of n-grams/LCS; often reported alongside ROUGE recall for fuller picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mismatch score (SEA-A regression)
rubrics_metrics.description: A regression-based mismatch score (SEA-A) that quantifies the consistency between a paper and a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computed by SEA-A trained on paper-review pairs. Larger mismatch scores indicate less consistency; Tables 7–8 compare random paper-review pairs vs corresponding pairs to validate the metric. Note: SEA-A was trained on a majority of low-scoring samples so absolute values may be small — interpret relative differences (e.g., random vs matching pairs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized review structure and content requirements (SEA-S instruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: When standardizing multiple reviews for one paper, the model should integrate them into three parts: textual descriptions (Summary, Strengths, Weaknesses, Questions), quantitative scores (Soundness, Presentation, Contribution, Rating), and review results; format should align with the original review template and incorporate the Area Chair's decision and corresponding acceptance/rejection reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction emphasizes: be rich and concise, avoid redundant information, preserve required fields and numeric scores, and generate clear acceptance/rejection reasons consistent with the AC decision. Anti-patterns observed: outputs that lack complete format (missing fields), sparse content (missing parts), over-extraction/repetition of original text, or failure to eliminate redundant phrases (e.g., repetitive 'Lack of'). Examples: Mistral-7B lacked complete format and had sparse content; GPT-3.5 often simply extracted original review content without deduplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality — Q1: Importance of the research question (SEA-E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer discuss the importance of the research question?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human and GPT raters scored this on a 1–10 scale (higher = better). Evaluators should look for explicit discussion of problem significance and context in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality — Q2: Originality of the paper (SEA-E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer discuss the originality of the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Expectation: review should evaluate novelty, situate work relative to prior art, and avoid generic praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality — Q3: Identification of strengths and weaknesses of the method
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer clearly identify the strengths and weaknesses of the method (study design, data collection and data analysis)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Good reviews provide concrete, method-level analysis (not just surface-level comments) with examples from the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality — Q4: Specific useful comments on writing, organization, tables and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer make specific useful comments on the writing, organization, tables and figures of the manuscript?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Look for actionable, precise suggestions (e.g., which figure is unclear, how to reorganize a section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality — Q5: Constructiveness of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Were the reviewer’s comments constructive?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Constructive reviews suggest improvements and avoid merely negative or vague criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality — Q6: Evidence and examples to substantiate comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer supply appropriate evidence using examples from the paper to substantiate their comments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Strong reviews quote or cite specific results/paragraphs to justify critiques or praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality — Q7: Comment on authors' interpretation of the results
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer comment on the author’s interpretation of the results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Useful reviews check whether conclusions follow from results and highlight possible misinterpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality — Q8: Objectivity and avoidance of bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the reviewer maintain objectivity and avoid bias in the review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Includes neutrality in tone, fairness in criticism, and not favoring acceptance/rejection for non-scientific reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality — Q9: Professional and appropriate language
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the language used by the reviewer professional and appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Language should be civil, precise, and suitable for academic peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality — Q10: Overall review quality (SEA-E)
rubrics_metrics.description: How would you rate the quality of this review overall?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10 as an aggregate judgment. Used to compare models across human and GPT raters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality — Top-1 selection (human evaluation addition)
rubrics_metrics.description: After anonymizing model names, experts select the best review for each paper (top-1 preference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used only in human evaluation (not performed by GPT due to context-length limits). Aggregated as percent preferred; used as a tie-breaking/preference metric (SEA-E was preferred in 90% of cases by experts in study).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized Content — Q1: Consolidation of similar points (SEA-S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did this review effectively consolidate similar points from the original reviews?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Expectation: merge redundant points, present unified statements rather than duplicated reviewer comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized Content — Q2: Objectivity and avoidance of bias (SEA-S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the review maintain objectivity and avoid bias?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Same standard as SEA-E Q8 but applied to the consolidated/standardized output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized Content — Q3: Usefulness of information (SEA-S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did this review contain a lot of useful information?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Emphasizes informativeness and actionable content in the standardized review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized Content — Q4: Repetitiveness (SEA-S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did this review contain a lot of repetitive content?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10; lower repetitiveness is better. Anti-patterns include verbatim duplication and overuse of phrases (e.g., excessive 'Lack of').

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized Content — Q5: Contradictions in the review (SEA-S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there any contradiction in this review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10; contradictions (e.g., praising and criticizing the same item without reconciliation) reduce quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized Content — Q6: Professional language in standardized review (SEA-S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the language used by the review professional and appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10; same expectation as SEA-E Q9 applied to the standardized summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized Content — Q7: Overall quality of the standardized review (SEA-S)
rubrics_metrics.description: How would you rate the quality of this review overall?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10; aggregate judgment of the standardized content quality; used to compare SEA-S against baselines (SEA-S scored highly on relevance, coherence, conciseness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting alignment with original review template
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated standardized reviews should follow formatting aligned with the original review template (field names, score labels, numeric scales).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit instruction: ensure textual sections (Summary/Strengths/Weaknesses/Questions), numeric score fields (Soundness/Presentation/Contribution/Rating) and review result fields are present and labeled consistently with the conference template. Missing fields or wrong labels are considered format errors (observed in some baseline outputs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and redundancy avoidance in generated reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated reviews should be concise and avoid redundant or duplicated content while covering necessary points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models should avoid splitting a single issue into multiple near-duplicate points or copying verbatim reviewer statements. Examples: Mistral-7B split one complexity issue into two (not concise); GPT-3.5 tended to over-extract and preserve redundant phrases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage and detail (comprehensiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated reviews should cover the paper broadly (method, experiments, strengths, weaknesses, questions) and include sufficient detail where needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEA-E/SEA-EA were noted to generate clearer viewpoints and ensure extensive coverage; random or shorter outputs lacked detail (M-7B-Random). Balance coverage with conciseness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment between review content and paper decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons generated for acceptance/rejection should be consistent with the paper content and with the AC decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction specifically asks models to incorporate AC decision and generate corresponding acceptance/rejection reasons. Anti-pattern: review weaknesses that conflict with the declared decision indicate inconsistency (observed in some baseline outputs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding 'pleasing humans' bias (leniency/over-acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated reviews/decisions should avoid systematic bias toward acceptance (i.e., tending to accept most papers to please humans).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnose via precision/recall tradeoffs: high recall + low precision signals leniency. SEA observed that M-7B had high recall (~97%) but poor precision, indicating over-acceptance; desirable models balance precision and recall.
